text:
Maya Patel: Starting a quick cross-team sync on error taxonomy and reliability dashboards. We need runtime+router+infra inputs so the console can show unified error rates (timeouts, 5xx variants, OOMs, degraded/fallback counts). Can eng-runtime, eng-sre, and eng-platform reps drop in here?

Jonathan Wu: +1. Right now signals are fragmented: router emits transport 5xx, runtime logs OOM/timeouts, infra has node oom counters. We need one mapping so alerts/dashboards are consistent.

Lina Ortega: Suggest we target three query surfaces: request-level (client-visible status), node-level (OOM/mem pressure), and feature-level (degraded/fallback events). Distinguish timeout (server-side compute timeout) vs client-cancelled vs queue-throttle.

Kevin Singh: Proposed canonical metrics (low-cardinality):
- requests_total
- request_errors_total{error_type} with error_type in [timeout, transport, server, model, oom, validation, fallback, rate_limited]
- request_duration_seconds (histogram)
- node_ooms_total
- degraded_fallbacks_total
Labels: route, region, status_family. High-card labels (model_version, rollout_id) only sampled.

Maya Patel: Who should emit what? Router vs runtime vs node exporter?

Jonathan Wu: My view: runtime emits request_duration_seconds and model-related errors (model_crash, model_oom). Router emits transport errors, rate limit events, and should copy request context headers into runtime so we retain route/rollout metadata. Node exporter emits node_ooms_total and mem_pressure signals. Console will join aggregated low-cardinality metrics for display.

Miguel Alvarez: We need a tiny header contract: router adds X-RL-ROLLOUT-ID and X-RL-CUSTOMER-TIER into forwarded requests so runtime can attach minimal tags or log them (or expose sampled metrics).

Priya Rao: Cardinality note: rollout_id and exact_model_version explode series. Options: 1) never put them on base Prom counters, 2) include them only on sampled metrics (configurable rate), or 3) push full-card data to a metrics backend that supports high-cardinality. For default dashboards use aggregated labels (route, model_family).

Lina Ortega: Agreed. Policy: low-cardinality labels on primary counters: route, region, status_family. High-cardinality labels only on traces/logs or sampled metrics (default sample 1%).

Kevin Singh: Naming consistency: use error_type canonical set so alerts map cleanly. status_family should be coarse (5xx/4xx/timeout/oom/fallback) for panels.

Maya Patel: Alerts proposal and tentative owners:
- Elevated 5xx rate (>1% over 5m) -> eng-runtime
- Node OOM storm (>3 oom events/min on same zone) -> eng-sre
- Fallback ratio >2% on prod routes (10m window) -> eng-platform/product
- High p99 latency (text-gen p99 >1.5s) -> eng-runtime
Runbooks need owners and run steps.

Jonathan Wu: Also add a metric_version label if we need to evolve label sets without breaking dashboards. And mark experimental labels with x_exp_.

Miguel Alvarez: Runtime example pseudo-metrics to implement:
request_errors_total{error_type="model", route="/v1/generate", region="us-west-2", status_family="5xx"} 1
request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="0.1", route="/v1/generate"} 100
model_out_of_memory_total{model_family="redwood-small", node_id="n-12"} 1

Kevin Singh: Example PromQL for error rate per route:
(sum by(route) (rate(request_errors_total{status_family="5xx"}[5m])) / sum by(route) (rate(requests_total[5m]))) * 100
Fallback ratio example:
(sum by(route) (rate(degraded_fallbacks_total[10m])) / sum by(route) (rate(requests_total[10m]))) * 100

Priya Rao: Dashboards: suggested panels
1) Topline: requests, overall error% by error_type, latency p50/p95/p99
2) Node health: node_ooms, mem_pressure, CPU
3) Feature reliability: fallback counts, fallback ratio by route/feature
4) Rollout card (sampled): reliability metrics for rollout_id
5) Recent traces table (sampled)

Lina Ortega: UX: console rollout card should show aggregated metrics with a sampled drilldown link to logs/traces where rollout_id appears. For customers with enterprise telemetry enable full-cardinality tagging.

Maya Patel: Implementation timeline (owners):
- Day 2: Kevin to publish metric list and labeling guidance
- End of week: Miguel to open runtime PR that emits low-card counters/histograms (with sampling hooks)
- End of week: Jonathan to update router to mirror context headers and emit route-level counters
- Next Tue: Priya to add node_ooms metric + skeleton alerts in infra repo
- Next Wed: Lina to produce Grafana layout mockups; eng-platform + eng-sre to own dashboards & alert rules
- Documentation + runbooks: eng-sre

Kevin Singh: I'll include cardinality best-practices and sampling knobs in the doc.

Priya Rao: Will draft runbooks for the four alerts and post to #incidents for review.

deploy-bot: grafana dashboard deploy queued (job id: 5571)

Maya Patel: Nice progress. If there are edge cases (client-cancel vs server-timeout, optimistic vs forced fallback), call them out in the metric doc. We'll reconvene after the PRs are up. :thumbsup:
